newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Mark in ascendant, Euro bourses take profits.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Mark in ascendant, Euro bourses take profits.

text.p: The mark advanced against the dollar and yen in European morning trading on Wednesday, while leading stock markets followed Wall Street's example, cashing in more profits after a record-breaking run.
The U.S. and Japanese currencies ceded ground to the mark as the German mark reached its highest level in more than 3-1/2 years against the yen.
Traders said a growing belief in the foreign exchange market that Japanese interest rates would stay low for a while was helping to boost the mark.

Reinforcing this view, Bank of Japan governor Yasuo Matsushita said that while the economy was growing gradually, it was unlikely to accelerate soon and market expectations of higher rates were receding.
The mark/yen rate shot through its previous 1996 high of 73.78 in early European business to hit a peak of 74.09.

"The mark/yen surge is the by-product of a market that has been very underweight (in) marks on the one hand, while getting constant noises from Japan about maintenance of low interest rates there," said Michael Burke, an economist at Citibank.
U.S. comments about the harm which a high dollar rate could have on trade jolted the U.S. currency against the yen but it later revived smartly from a low of 112.04 yen to nearer 113.
U.S. stocks traded in London were mixed and brokers said Wall Street might see another day of profit-taking after falling on Tuesday amid concern about corporate earnings.
"There isn't much interest here," said one London broker. "The market feels weak."

Whatever Wall Street's immediate prospects, investors pondering whether the world's biggest stock market can add to its heady gains were given encouragement by Steven Einhorn, partner and head of global investment research at Goldman Sachs.
Speaking in Hong Kong, he said the bull market that has swept U.S. share prices to record levels should continue into 1998 and European equities could do even better.
European bourses had already taken the New York market's slip into account in afternoon business on Tuesday, but Frankfurt in particular lost more ground when trading resumed.
The DAX index of 30 German blue chips was dragged down by a plunge of almost a quarter in the shares of business software firm SAP after a profits warning.
With little scheduled company news on the agenda and investors having lost some of their enthusiasm for a new buying spree, the London stock market also declined.
Pearson shares hit a record high of 752 pence after recent bid speculation and management changes. But by 1100 GMT they were trading 7-1/2 pence lower at 735.

The Paris bourse also started in deficit following the dip on Wall Street and weakness in the dollar and bonds. Shares in resorts group Club Mediterranee, which issued a profits warning late on Tuesday, fell by almost a fifth.
CURRENCIES AT 1100 GMT
The dollar was trading around 1.5250 marks and 112.95 yen, compared with Tuesday's late European levels of 1.5347 and 112.83 yen.
STOCKS AT 1100 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 11.1 points at 4,046.1.
Frankfurt's 30-share DAX index was 18.39 lower at 2,700.59.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index lost 8.01 to 2,167.60.
PRECIOUS METALS

Gold was fixed at $383.95 an ounce in the morning and later rose to around $384.30, up from $383.65 at the London close on Tuesday. Traders reported increasingly bullish market sentiment. Silver added two cents to $4.99.
